chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from Thaʿlabah ibn Maymūn, from Muḥammad ibn Muḍārib, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

There is no objection to a masjid being made over excrement. Thus, this does not contradict the first report, because the proper way to reconcile the two is that it is only permissible for it to be made a masjid when it has been covered with earth and the odor has ceased. This is indicated by that.

key_terms.الرَّائِحَةُ: the odor whose disappearance is a condition for permissibility
key_terms.الْخَبَرَ الْأَوَّلَ: the earlier report with which this narration is being reconciled
key_terms.الْعَذِرَةِ: excrement or filth over which the masjid is discussed
key_terms.بِالتُّرَابِ: with earth, meaning the filth is covered by soil
key_terms.مَسْجِدٌ: a place of sajdah or masjid being established on the site

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to build a masjid over a place of excrement if it is covered and the odor is gone?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on establishing a masjid over a place of filth. It explains that permissibility is conditioned on the area being covered with earth and the smell having disappeared, thereby reconciling apparently differing reports on the matter.
